q: How many doors are on this floor?
note: An apartment building in Tallinn: 5 floor plans and the 3D model. Ask the way you talk. The answer comes first, with where it comes from, numbered on the plan.

q: Which is the biggest room on this floor?
note: Rooms too: the biggest one, the next ones, and each of them marked. Click a line to zoom to it.

q: How many windows in the whole building?
note: The whole building at once, from the 3D model: every window counted and lit up.

q: How many windows on floor 1 are in the 3D model but not drawn on this plan?
note: Differences found: the drawings and the 3D model are checked against each other, floor by floor. Here 3 windows sit above the height where the plan is cut. One click shows them.
A floor plan from Switzerland: the size of one apartment, with its rooms marked, in a fraction of a second instead of a quarter of an hour by hand.

q: Wie viele Türen und Fenster sind insgesamt auf diesem Grundriss eingezeichnet?
note: Any language: asked in German, answered and marked the same way.
A scanned Finnish apartment plan, read from the image alone.
Old drawings too: a historic survey sheet, answered from its own title block, the line it read marked.
How accurate is it? Measured on drawings the system never saw while it was built, against simpler approaches, with the cost per question.
